cap: hCG from the syncytiotrophoblast doubles about every 48 hours, peaks near 10 weeks and then falls to a low plateau. It keeps the corpus luteum making progesterone until the luteal-placental shift at 7 to 10 weeks, after which the placenta supplies it alone. Human placental lactogen rises with placental mass, so insulin resistance is greatest late in pregnancy.
teach: Read the three lanes against the same week scale. The hCG curve explains why a home test turns positive within days and why nausea is worst near 10 weeks. The progesterone lane explains why removing the corpus luteum before the shift can end a pregnancy but removing it later cannot. The hPL ramp explains why gestational diabetes is screened for at 24 to 28 weeks rather than at the first visit.
